 Naushad Moosa’s SAFF Journey Comes Full Circle
 From winning the SAFF Championship as a player in 1997 to leading India as head coach in 2026, Naushad Moosa returns to familiar territory with a depleted squad and a new challenge By Rahul Giri November 5, 2026 No Comments 4 Mins Read

 As defending champions India begin their SAFF Championship 2026 campaign against arch-rivals Pakistan in Dhaka, Bangladesh, head coach Naushad Moosa completes a full circle. Having won the competition as a player in 1997, after finishing runners-up in 1995, Moosa now returns to the regional tournament at the helm of the Blue Tigers. He was a resolute presence in the backline when India finished runners-up in Sri Lanka, before helping them clinch silverware two years later in Nepal, where they defeated the Maldives 5-1 in the final. 
 With the AIFF opting to send the senior team to New Zealand under head coach Khalid Jamil for two friendly matches celebrating 100 years of sporting ties between the two nations, Moosa has been entrusted with the squad for this regional tournament, with Bibiano Fernandes serving as his deputy. 
 During his playing career, Moosa was a formidable defender who represented major clubs, including East Bengal FC, Mahindra United, Mohammedan Sporting and Air India. Across a career spanning nearly two decades, he earned 42 international caps for India. Once his playing career came to a close, he did not rush towards immediate high-profile assignments. Instead, he undertook a patient, step-by-step coaching apprenticeship that established him as one of the country’s most respected minds in youth development. 
 Moosa is widely regarded as one of India’s finest coaches when it comes to identifying young talent and grooming players for the senior level. Having served as head of youth development at Bengaluru FC and currently holding a similar role at NorthEast United FC, he has overseen the transition of several young prospects into top-flight professionals. 
 Under his guidance, the Indian U-23 team narrowly missed out on qualification for the AFC U-23 Asian Cup but put in a promising display in Qatar. The upcoming SAFF Championship presents another crucial test for the former India international, accompanied by a unique set of challenges. 
 For India’s opening fixture against Pakistan, Moosa will have only 17 players available for selection, including just two goalkeepers. The remaining players will join the squad in Dhaka only after the conclusion of Indian Super League Matchweek 5 on 7 November. In fact, India’s initial training sessions in Kolkata featured just one goalkeeper on the pitch, Priyansh Dubey. 
 Adding to the challenge, Pakistan present a very different proposition from the side India thrashed 4-0 in their last SAFF Championship meeting in 2023. Although most of their players based abroad, who compete in the lower tiers of European leagues, will only be available if Pakistan reach the knockout stages, as the group matches fall outside the FIFA international window, their domestic squad still possesses enough quality to push India to their limits. 
 “We are going to face a different Pakistan team compared to the one we faced in the last SAFF Championship, and we are definitely prepared for that,” Moosa said during the pre-match press conference. “We would certainly like to win the match. I don’t think there is any particular pressure. Rather, it is about having the motivation to give our best and put everything on the pitch. Hopefully, we can come away with a good result.” 
 Despite the squad constraints, Moosa remains determined to secure his first major trophy as national team head coach while shielding his young squad from unnecessary expectations. 
 “We are defending the title, and we are playing away from home, here in Bangladesh,” he said. “As I said, I have come here with a young team because we also have friendly matches against New Zealand, with one squad (led by senior national team head coach Khalid Jamil) travelling there to play two games.  
 “What is important to me is that my players play with a free mind. I am not really worried about defending the title. What I am concerned about is playing good football. When the team plays good football, the results will follow.” 
 The tournament, therefore, is more than just another coaching assignment for Moosa. Navigating player shortages, integrating players and managing regional rivalries will not be easy. But if he can translate the composure and expertise of his playing days into this young side, India’s SAFF title defence might just mark the beginning of an exciting new chapter for the Blue Tigers.
